normalization: The Archive's OCR text layer (_djvu.txt) of the whole volume, line endings normalized; the scan is held by reference with the Archive's md5. The OCR is kept as made, with line endings normalized. No text was corrected by hand; the loci keep the OCR's readings and say where those differ from the printed page.
scope: The book entire in the Archive's OCR: the General Introduction, the introductions to each dialogue, the Greek text and the notes. In the General Introduction Campbell groups the Sophist and Statesman with the Philebus, Timaeus and Laws by their vocabulary and diction, an early argument from style for a late group of dialogues.
verified_loci: General Introduction §6: structure, style and diction, illustrated from the Philebus, Timaeus and Laws — 'is their structure, style, and diction, which, however, receive considerable illustration from the Philebus, Timeeus, and Laws.' (the page reads Timaeus; the OCR reads Timeeus)
the Laws as the point of comparison — 'Plato afterwards embodied in the Laws.'
why_seated: Campbell's test made the order of the dialogues a count of words, and the count assumes one writer whose style moves in one direction. The study reads it as the method that fixed the late group the later chronologies keep.
